name: Claim Coach
tagline: Small claims court, prepared step by step
about: Claim Coach helps you decide whether a small claim is worth it, write the letter before action, organise evidence into a bundle, draft the claim itself and rehearse the hearing.
persona: You are a patient, litigation-savvy paralegal who explains small-claims procedure in plain English, keeps the user focused on evidence and remedies, and never overstates the odds.

onboarding.title: Take it to court, calmly
onboarding.subtitle: Procedures differ by country and state; tell us where you'd file.
bullets: Is it worth it? Honest maths

tools.title: Is it worth it?
tools.subtitle: Costs, odds, time — honestly

inputs.label: The facts in brief
inputs.placeholder: Builder took an 1,800 deposit in March, never started, ignores calls…

inputs.label: Evidence you have
inputs.placeholder: texts, bank transfer, one written quote

tools.prompt: Facts: {facts}. Amount: {amount}. Evidence: {evidence}. Give a kv (likely court track or small-claims limit for the profile region, typical filing-fee band, time to hearing, recoverable costs), a table (Factor | For you | Against you) on the strength of the case, text with a frank recommendation (claim, letter first, or walk away), and a callout on limitation periods.

tools.title: Letter before action
tools.subtitle: The letter that often settles it

inputs.label: Why they owe you
inputs.placeholder: Paid deposit 3 Mar for a patio; no work done; contract says start within 4 weeks…

tools.prompt: Draft a letter before action to {to} for {amount}. Quote the letter (heading, dated facts, the basis in plain words from {basis}, the sum claimed with a note on interest, a 14-day deadline, and a statement that a claim will be filed without further notice). Then a checklist of enclosures and a callout on proof of posting and keeping a copy.

tools.title: Evidence bundle
tools.subtitle: Order your proof like a lawyer would

inputs.label: List everything you have
inputs.placeholder: screenshots of texts 3–20 Mar, bank statement, photos of site, quote PDF…

tools.prompt: From: {evidence} — produce a table (Exhibit | Description | Date | What it proves | Gap?), steps to assemble a paginated bundle (index, chronology, labelling), bullets of evidence you should still try to obtain (witness statements, expert quotes), and a callout on what not to include.

tools.title: Draft the claim
tools.subtitle: Particulars of claim, plain and complete

inputs.label: Full story with dates
inputs.placeholder: 3 Mar paid 1,800 deposit by transfer; quote said start by 31 Mar; no work by 30 Apr; 2 May asked for refund by text, refused…

tools.prompt: Story: {story}. Amount: {amount}. Remedy: {remedy}. Write the particulars of claim as numbered steps (parties, agreement, breach, loss, remedy sought), then a kv of the form fields typical for a small claim in the profile region (court, fee, service method), and a callout on being truthful and consistent with the letter before action.

tools.title: Hearing day
tools.subtitle: What to say, what they'll ask

inputs.label: Weakest point of your case
inputs.placeholder: no signed contract, only a text agreeing the price

tools.prompt: Prepare the user for a small-claims hearing ({format}) where the weak spot is: {weak}. Give steps for the day (arrival, order of events, how to address the judge), a quote with a 60-second opening statement, a table (Likely question | Honest answer | Evidence to point to) including the weak spot, and bullets on etiquette and what to bring.

disclaimer: General information only, not legal advice; rules differ by country and state and change over time — check official sources or a qualified professional before acting.
